description: The image displays two concentric circular charts, each illustrating a hierarchical classification of educational content, with the right chart labeled “FineWeb-Edu Classifier.” The outer ring of each chart represents broad educational categories, while the inner ring breaks them down into more specific subcategories, each annotated with a numerical value. The left chart shows categories such as “Education” (25), “Science & technology education” (10), “Teaching & resources” (15), “Health & Medicine” (22), “Diseases” (11), “Nutrition” (5), “Medical” (6), “Science” (15), “Animal & Plant” (13), “Historical review” (7), “Society & culture” (10), “Events & people” (6), “Materials” (2), “Infor tech” (5), “Emerging tech” (4), “Manage” (2), “Policy” (1), “Fin & Law” (3), and “Tech & Engineer” (12). The right chart presents a similar structure but with different numerical values for the same or similar categories: “Education” (38), “Teaching & resources” (17), “Science & technology education” (19), “Health & Medicine” (19), “Diseases” (10), “Nutrition” (7), “Medical” (2), “Animal & Plant” (12), “Science” (15), “Historical review” (12), “Society & culture” (5), “Events & people” (2), “Materials” (3), “Infor tech” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Manage” (1), “Policy” (1), “Fin & Law” (3), and “Tech & Engineer” (8). Both charts use color-coding for the outer segments (e.g., teal for Education, blue for Health & Medicine, red for Science) and the inner segments (e.g., orange for History & Society, pink for Animal & Plant). Each segment is labeled with its category name and a number, presumably indicating the count or weight of that category within the dataset. The charts appear to be comparing the distribution of topics in two different versions or datasets, likely for analysis of educational content classification. There are no percentage labels inside the slices, no legend, and no visual emphasis such as exploded slices. The segments in both charts are arranged in a clockwise order, generally from largest to smallest within each ring, though not strictly sorted.
